source: NCERT Class IX, Contemporary India I, Geography Ch. 6.

sections.heading: 1. Population — Size and Distribution
points: **Census** (held every **10 years**) counts the population; India is the **most populous** country (over **1.4 billion**).
Population distribution is **very uneven** — depends on **relief, climate, soil, water, industry and urbanisation**.
**Uttar Pradesh** is the most populous state; the Northern Plains and coasts are densely populated; deserts and mountains sparsely.

sections.heading: 2. Density and Growth
points: **Population density** = persons per sq km (India ≈ **382/sq km**, 2011).
**Growth of population** = change over time (natural increase = births − deaths; plus migration).
The **annual growth rate** has been **declining**, but numbers keep rising due to the large base.

sections.heading: 3. Population Composition
points: **Age structure** — children (0–14), working age (15–59), aged (60+); India has a large **young population** (a 'demographic dividend').
**Sex ratio** = number of **females per 1000 males** (a social indicator).
**Literacy rate**, **occupational structure** (primary/secondary/tertiary) and **health** (life expectancy, IMR) describe the quality of the population.
The **adolescent** population is large and needs special attention (nutrition, education).

sections.heading: 4. Population Policy
points: The **National Population Policy (NPP) 2000** aims to stabilise population and improve health, education and welfare.
It provides free education (to 14), reduces infant mortality, promotes immunisation and small families.
Investing in **health and education** turns a large population into a productive **human resource**.

sections.heading: 5. High-Yield One-Liners (Last-Minute Recall)
points: Census every 10 years; India = most populous country; UP = most populous state.
Density = persons per sq km (India ≈ 382/sq km, 2011).
Growth = natural increase (births − deaths) + migration; growth rate declining.
Sex ratio = females per 1000 males; India has a large young population (demographic dividend).
National Population Policy 2000 = stabilise population + health/education.

sections.heading: 6. Common Traps (Watch Out)
points: **Population density = persons per square kilometre** (not total).
**Sex ratio = females per 1000 males**.
India's **growth RATE is falling**, but total population still rises (large base).
The **National Population Policy** was adopted in **2000**.
